confidence_notes: The FX figure is the RBA AUD/USD representative rate of 0.6720 as at 18 November 2026, taken from search results that quoted the RBA exchange-rate pages. Food and drink anchors come from city-level aggregator figures found in search. Beer (about US$2.4) and cappuccino (about US$3.7, backed by a Querétaro menu price of MX$66) have the most support. Restaurant meal figures varied across sources, some of them dated 2023, so I chose values within the reported ranges. I found no reliable Querétaro cocktail or wine prices. Cocktail is set at about 2.5 times beer and wine glass at about 2.2 times beer, based on typical Mexican restaurant pricing. I did not search for accommodation. Those four anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge of Querétaro as a mid-sized business and tourism city with a colonial historic centre, and they are the least certain.
comparable_city_reasoning: Comparable to other Mexican colonial and business cities such as Guanajuato, San Miguel de Allende (somewhat pricier) and Puebla. It is cheaper than Mexico City's trendy districts but more expensive than the typical Mexican provincial city.
